items.title: Sharp, smooth trailers
items.text: Trailers on title pages and behind the Discover banner played in blurry low quality, because YouTube picks the quality from how big the player is and ours were small. They now ask for full HD, and the frosted buttons over a playing banner trailer turn plain so the video doesn't stutter.

items.title: One trailer at a time
items.text: The banner trailer kept playing out of sight when you scrolled down or opened a title, so a title page's trailer had to share the computer with it. It now stops as soon as you can't see it and starts again when you come back.

title: Deleting a season stops its download

items.title: No more waiting for a download you deleted
items.text: Deleting a season or a show while it was still downloading only removed the finished episodes, and the rest kept downloading and came back. Delete now cancels the download and any conversion straight away, and the season's Delete button shows up even before the first episode is ready.

items.title: Trailer and title side by side
items.text: On a computer a playing trailer filled the whole window and pushed the title off the bottom. It now plays in a frame on top of the blurred picture, with the title still in view below.

items.title: Trailer on wide screens
items.text: On a computer the Trailer button on a title's page could sit under the title text, so clicking it did nothing. It's on top now and plays the trailer.

title: Finished downloads become playable right away

items.title: No more stuck "Almost ready"
items.text: A film's page left open while it downloaded could stay on "Almost ready 100%" after it finished, and you had to reload to play it. The page now switches to the film by itself.

title: Play now shows how long until it starts

items.title: Clearer Play now wait
items.text: While Play now gets the start of a video, the percentage and time now count toward starting playback, not the whole download. So you see "40% · about 30 s to go" instead of "0% downloaded · about 2 h left".

title: Big downloads don't stall at the start

items.title: No more "moving" pause
items.text: A big download could stop for a few minutes just after it started while the server shuffled it to a faster drive (Lost in Translation sat at 4 %). New downloads now start on that drive straight away, so they keep going.

title: Undo, thumbs down that counts, and more

items.title: Thumbs down hides it
items.text: Titles you give a thumbs down no longer show up in your Discover rows, Documentaries or Popular on Lilin. Search still finds them, and taking the thumbs down back brings them back.

items.title: Undo after deleting
items.text: After you delete something, you get a few seconds to press Undo before it's really gone.

items.title: Play now is on its way
items.text: While a download fetches the start of the video, it says so ("Play now in a moment"), so you know the Play now button is coming.

items.title: Tidy Continue watching
items.text: Each Continue watching card has a ⋯ button: Mark as watched, or Remove from Continue watching (your place is kept and it comes back when you watch it again).

items.title: Night mode remembers the show
items.text: Turn on night mode during a show and it's on again for that show's next episodes. Other shows and films start with it off.

items.title: Stray "false" text
items.text: Some sheets, like Browse while you're in Documentaries, showed the word "false" where nothing should be. Gone everywhere.

items.title: English documentaries only
items.text: With Lilin in English, Documentaries now only shows titles that were made in English: the SVT Play, Swedish and Nordic rows are gone, and the other rows leave out foreign-language films and shows. With Lilin in Swedish nothing changes.

items.title: Documentary genres on phones
items.text: The genre rows under Documentaries were wider than a phone screen, so the whole page shrank and the posters looked tiny. The rows now fit and swipe sideways, and the page is full size again.

items.title: Removed films
items.text: When a film you have open leaves your library, its page now shows a tidy card with a Back to your library button instead of a bare heading on a coloured background.

items.title: Featurettes stay out of your library
items.text: Downloads that came with bonus material (featurettes, interviews, trailers) listed each bonus video as another "version" of the film, and Delete all versions didn't go through. Bonus folders are now left out of the library, and deleting the film removes them with it.

title: Film pages stay put, X closes once

items.title: No false "Removed from your library"
items.text: A film page left open while Lilin finished preparing the film for playback could suddenly say "Removed from your library" and lose its Delete button, even though nothing was removed. It now keeps showing the film.

items.title: Tapping X twice
items.text: Tapping the X on a page twice in a row could take you out of Lilin altogether (on iPad it could close the tab). A second tap now does nothing.

items.title: Delete right after downloading
items.text: Deleting a film or episode that had only just finished downloading could quietly fail while Lilin was still preparing it for playback. Delete now stops that preparation and removes it straight away.

title: Play now shows up when there's something to play

items.title: Play now waits for the start
items.text: The Play now button on a download now only appears once the beginning of the video has actually arrived, so pressing it no longer leaves you staring at a loading screen while the download hasn't really started. New downloads fetch the start first, so it usually shows up within seconds.

title: Night mode no longer turns the sound up

items.title: Quieter night mode
items.text: Switching on night mode (the moon in the player) used to make everything louder at once. Now dialogue stays about as loud as before and loud scenes like explosions and music come down, so you can keep the volume low without missing what people say.

title: Let people you trust invite others

items.title: Can invite people
items.text: In People, each person now has a Can invite people switch (off for everyone). Switched on, they get Invite people in their Settings and can make the same one-time links you make, up to 3 open at a time. Their links show up in your invite list with their name, and you can cancel them there.

title: Tidier likes on Popular on Lilin

items.title: No more cut-off names
items.text: Cards in Popular on Lilin no longer cut a list of names in half. A title liked by one person shows their name; liked by more, it shows their faces and how many liked it. Hold the pointer over it, or open the title, to see everyone.

title: Documentaries in English start with English titles

items.title: English titles first
items.text: With Lilin set to English, the Documentaries tab now starts with international true crime, unsolved cases, nature and history. SVT Play and Swedish true crime are still there, further down the page.

title: Clips: adding your camera is about 6x faster

items.title: Camera edits in about a minute
items.text: Putting your camera on top of a clip used to take several minutes, because the server redid the whole picture on its processor. It now uses the graphics card, so a full clip is done in about a minute, with the same picture quality.

title: Clips: edits in progress stay out of the list

items.title: No broken clip while a trim saves
items.text: While a trim or edit was still being saved, its unfinished file showed up in Clips as a clip of its own, with no picture and errors when you opened it. It now stays hidden until the edit is done.

title: 4K Dolby Vision episodes play on the Samsung TV

items.title: No more "can't play" error
items.text: Some 4K episodes (like The Rings of Power) stopped on the Samsung TV with an error, because the TV can't read how their video is labelled. The TV now gets a copy it can play. The first time you press Play on one of these it may load for a minute or two while that copy is made; after that it starts right away.

items.title: No more floating cards
items.text: The card that pops up when you rest the mouse on a title could sometimes stay stuck on the screen and float along as you scrolled, mostly after switching to another tab and back. It now closes when you leave the tab or window, and scrolling always closes it.

items.title: Plus sign is back
items.text: The Add button on the card that pops up when you hover over a title, and on the big banner at the top of Home, was missing its plus sign and showed an empty gap. The plus is back.

items.title: No more letter columns
items.text: When a letter, poster or sign in an anime shows Japanese text, the subtitles' translation of it sometimes came out as a long column of single letters or a pile of pieces in the middle of the picture. Those translations now show as one short line at the top of the screen, and the dialogue stays at the bottom.

items.title: One season at a time
items.text: Download several seasons of a show and they now come one after another, lowest season first, so the next one to watch finishes sooner. The rest show as queued. If two people download different seasons of the same show, each person's next season runs at the same time.

items.title: Honorifics show properly
items.text: Some anime subtitles showed names like "Yui{**-san}". They now read "Yui-san", and translator comments hidden in the subtitle file no longer show up on screen.

items.title: Scanning mistakes fixed by AI
items.text: Every English subtitle in the library is now read through once by an AI model on the desktop's graphics card, which fixes the mistakes left by subtitles that were scanned off a disc, like "iysteria in the cream cheese" (Listeria) or "the Wizard of 02". Only fixes that look like scanning mistakes are kept, never rewordings. What you're watching and the next episode go first. It waits while CS2 is running and when the desktop is off.

title: Subtitles check their spelling of names

items.title: Names learned from another subtitle
items.text: When an episode's English subtitles get names wrong, Lilin now fetches a second English subtitle of the same episode in the background and copies how it writes names, films and brands ("Shyamalan", "a large Coke", "Star Wars"). Only the capital letters change: the words and timing stay the ones that match your video. The next episode's is fetched while you watch.

items.title: Names and typos fixed in more subtitles
items.text: Some subtitles write characters' names in lowercase ("talk to cuddy") or come with scanning mistakes. Lilin now uses each show's and film's cast list to put names right, even when every release of the show gets them wrong. It also fixes split words ("w rong"), stray spaces ("he' s"), run-together numbers ("$12,0001967") and single letters ("vitamin c", "flying v"). Subtitles that were already fine stay as they are.

title: See your camera edits being made

items.title: Camera edits in progress
items.text: While your camera is being put into an edited copy, the clip now says so in Clips, with how far it has got, and the editor tells you too. If you save the same clip again before it's done, Lilin stops the first one and only makes your newest edit. Before, both ran at once and could spoil each other's copy.

title: Put your camera in your clips

items.title: Camera in the clip editor
items.text: Clips recorded while the OBS virtual camera is on now come with your camera. In the clip editor it shows as a box on the picture: drag it anywhere, pull its corner to make it bigger or smaller, and switch it on or off under Overlay, like the audio tracks. Saving with the camera on puts it in the copy in full quality, which takes a few minutes; you get a message when it's in Trimmed Clips.

items.title: No more stuck seasons from fake files
items.text: Sometimes a download that looks like a new episode is really a program pretending to be one. Lilin never opens it. It now removes the download on its own and gets a real copy of that episode instead, and the rest of the season keeps downloading in the meantime.

items.title: Ratings that match your language
items.text: Title pages sometimes showed the Swedish age rating (like Btl or 15) even with Lilin in English. In English you now see the American rating, or the British one when there's no American rating. In Swedish you still see the Swedish rating.

title: Fullscreen on iPhone keeps Lilin's player

items.title: Lilin from your Home Screen
items.text: On iPhone, the fullscreen button used to swap Lilin's player for Apple's, which has no Skip intro, Up next or Watch Together. In Safari it now shows three quick steps to add Lilin to your Home Screen, where the player fills the whole screen with everything still working. Apple's player is still one tap away in the same place if you prefer it.

items.title: Complete seasons in one go
items.text: Some complete-season downloads were thrown away because of how their files were named, so Lilin fetched the episodes one by one instead, with gaps. Those complete seasons are now kept and downloaded whole.

items.title: Clearer message
items.text: When an episode can't be found, Lilin now says "not found yet" instead of "not out yet".

items.title: Same library, new name
items.text: The app is now called Lilin, with a new address and a new icon. Your library, watch progress, lists, notes and rooms are all still here. Old links, bookmarks and invites still work: they take you to the new address.

items.title: Sign in once more
items.text: Because the address changed, you'll be asked to sign in one more time on each device. After that everything works as before.

items.title: New icon on your home screen
items.text: If you added the app to your phone's home screen, remove it and add it again from the new address to get the new name and icon. The TV apps get them with their next update.

items.title: Fewer pauses while things download
items.text: Downloads in progress and video conversions now happen on a faster drive and only move to the library once they're done. Videos you're watching should stop pausing to load while other things are downloading.

items.title: Everyone hears the host's language
items.text: When the host of a Watch Together room picks another audio language, everyone in the room switches to it, also people who join later. Anyone can still pick their own language with the Audio button; that stays just theirs, and the room keeps playing while they switch.

items.title: Your language starts in a second or two
items.text: Picking another audio language used to mean waiting minutes while Lilin made a copy of the whole video. Now the language you pick plays right away, at up to 1080p, from the same spot. When the full-quality copy is ready, the player moves back to it by itself.

items.title: New Audio button
items.text: The audio language button in the player now has the usual translate icon.

title: Pop-out from the Home Screen app

items.title: Picture in picture hands over to Safari
items.text: iPhone doesn't allow picture in picture in apps added to the Home Screen, only in Safari. In the Home Screen app, the pop-out button now opens the same video in Safari at the same second: press play there, then pop it out.

items.title: Pop the video out on iPhone and Android
items.text: The picture-in-picture button now shows up and works on iPhone and iPad too, and subtitles carry over into the small window. On Android, leaving the browser while a film plays pops it out by itself.

items.title: English search keyboard
items.text: On an Android TV that isn’t set to Swedish, the search keyboard no longer has å, ä and ö. It has an apostrophe, & and ! instead, for titles like Schindler’s List.

items.title: The Android TV app keeps itself up to date
items.text: On Android 12 and later, the Lilin app now updates by itself: a new version downloads in the background and installs when you’re not using the app. Update it once more when it asks (version 1.2.0), and allow Lilin to install apps if the TV asks; after that there’s nothing to press.

items.title: Arrows on the cast row
items.text: On a computer, the cast on a title page now has the same arrows as the other rows, so you can scroll through everyone without a trackpad. They hide when every face already fits.

items.title: Clipper setup no longer needs Python
items.text: node setup.js clipper now installs Clipper 0.2, which is written in Rust: no Python on the gaming PC, and its benchmark on Windows no longer installs Python either. Its programs come from Clipper's release and are checked against fixed checksums before they run, the same way the source already was.

items.title: Names fit again in the People list
items.text: On a phone, the Password link and Remove buttons squeezed each person’s name and details into a narrow column, one letter per line. The buttons now sit underneath on small screens, so names, emails and last-seen details read normally.

items.title: The Android TV app works away from home
items.text: The Lilin app for Android TV and Google TV now works on any TV with internet, not just at home, so friends and family elsewhere can use it too. Get it from Settings → Android TV, sign the TV in with the code from your phone, and it carries on as before. It speaks English, or Swedish when the TV is set to Swedish. A TV that already has the app offers the update when it starts.

items.title: A faster Samsung TV app
items.text: The Samsung TV app has been rebuilt from the ground up so it runs much lighter on the TV. Moving around, scrolling rows and opening titles is quicker and smoother, and everything else works as before: Home, Discover, Search, Skip intro, Up next and subtitles. You stay signed in. If the new app ever can't start on a TV, the old one opens instead.

items.title: A Lilin app for Android TV
items.text: Lilin now has an app for Android TV and Google TV: Chromecast with Google TV, Nvidia Shield and TVs with Google TV built in. It looks and works just like the Samsung app. To put it on a TV, open Settings → Android TV on your phone at home and follow the steps. It takes a few minutes, and the app keeps itself up to date after that.

items.title: Names and details fit again
items.text: In Settings → People, each person's name, email and storage sit on one line again, with their switches and library choice underneath, instead of being squeezed into a narrow column.

items.title: Change password looks the part
items.text: In Settings → You, Change password is now a proper row: tap it to open the form, tap again to close it.

items.title: Updates come as a notification
items.text: When Lilin gets something new, your phone or computer gets a notification with a quick summary. Tap it to read the whole note. Don't want them? Turn off Lilin updates in Settings → Notifications.

items.title: Discover feels like a cinema
items.text: Trending titles now fill the top of the screen, one at a time, with their own title art. On a computer the trailer starts playing quietly after a moment. Swipe between them on your phone.

items.title: Rows made for you
items.text: Discover now starts with what you're watching and what's on its way, then picks based on what you watched last, new things in your library and a few moods that change every day.

items.title: Bigger title pages
items.text: Opening a film or show gives it the whole screen: its title art, how long it is, the age rating, the cast with their faces, every episode with a picture and a short description, and More like this.

items.title: A quick look without opening
items.text: On a computer, rest the mouse on a poster for a moment to see more. On a phone, press and hold a poster.

items.title: Watch Together is simpler
items.text: No more Ready button or start times: open a room, invite someone, and when they're in, press Play. Everyone starts together.

items.title: Tidier everywhere else
items.text: A bigger layout on computers and TVs, Settings in clear groups, cleaner player menus, and the sign-in and invite pages in the same style.

title: Sign in with your own password

items.title: No more codes by email
items.text: Lilin now signs you in with your email and your own password instead of a code sent to your inbox. If you haven't picked a password yet, Lilin asks for one the next time you open it. On a new phone or computer, sign in with that email and password.

items.title: Invites sign people straight in
items.text: Someone you invite picks a password on the invite page and goes straight into Lilin, with no Cloudflare login to explain.

items.title: Password links
items.text: In People, anyone who still has no password shows "No password yet". Press Password link and send it to them: it only lets them set the password for their own email.

items.title: Start a room before the download finishes
items.text: When you watch something with Play now, the Watch together button is there too. Everyone in the room watches the download as it comes in, and they don't need it in their own library.

items.title: It waits instead of stuttering
items.text: If the download falls behind, the room pauses for everyone at the same moment and says it's waiting for the download, with a rough time when it can. It carries on together once there's enough to keep going.

items.title: Full quality for the whole room
items.text: When the download finishes, whoever hosts the room can press Switch now. Everyone moves to the full-quality video from the same spot, with subtitles and every audio track.

items.title: No more stutter at the start of a trimmed clip
items.text: Clips you trimmed in Lilin used to freeze and buffer for a second or two at the start, then suddenly play normally. New trims now play smoothly from the first frame, and they still start on exactly the frame you picked, at full quality.

items.title: Skip intro works on more episodes
items.text: Some episodes play for a long time before their opening titles, like one in Better Call Saul that runs over nine minutes. Lilin now finds those titles too, so the Skip intro button shows up.

items.title: No more stopping for small hiccups
items.text: A short hiccup for one person no longer pauses the video for the whole room. They catch up on their own, and the room only waits if the problem lasts longer than a second.

items.title: Steadier sound and picture
items.text: Everyone's video now adjusts its timing far less often, which should keep the sound lined up with the picture. If it still drifts, pausing and playing again fixes it.

items.title: Fewer interruptions
items.text: Videos still downloading now start with a bigger head start when the download is quick. If the download falls behind, playback pauses once to catch up instead of stopping every few seconds.

items.title: Episodes from season packs
items.text: An episode you play while its season downloads now arrives in order, so it starts sooner and stops less.

title: Play now: watch while it downloads

items.title: No more waiting for the download
items.text: Press Play now on anything that's still downloading and it starts as soon as the first part has arrived, on any device. It plays at up to 1080p, without subtitles or a choice of audio, until the download is done.

items.title: If it has to buffer
items.text: When the video catches up with the download, a popup tells you why and how far along the download is. Skipping ahead past what has downloaded waits until the download gets there. For smooth playback in full quality, wait for the download to finish. When it does, you can switch over from the same spot.

items.title: Cast names are links
items.text: Press an actor’s name under a description to open their TMDB page and see what else they’ve been in.

items.title: Cast under the description
items.text: Films and shows now list their main actors right under the description, in the app and on the TV.

title: Upgrade quality moved to where you need it

items.title: Right in the player
items.text: Episode looks soft? Open the Quality button in the player and press Upgrade quality. It replaces the season with a clearly better copy, and your place carries over.

items.title: And on the season’s page
items.text: It also sits next to the season’s episode count, instead of inside More episodes.

items.title: Tidier Audio choice
items.text: Choosing Dubbed on an anime no longer pushes the Episodes box out of line.

title: Best Quality now really goes for the best picture

items.title: Picked by picture, not popularity
items.text: Best Quality looks at where a release came from and how much of the picture survived. An untouched disc copy comes first, and a small popular re-encode no longer wins because more people share it. These downloads are bigger and can take longer.

items.title: No more odd versions
items.text: 3D, AI-upscaled and disc-image releases are skipped on every quality setting, unless nothing else exists.

title: Old seasons no longer say Not released

items.title: Every aired season can be chosen
items.text: Some shows, like One Piece, wrongly showed seasons from years ago as Not released, so you couldn't pick them. They can now be chosen and added, on the TV app as well.

items.title: Choose Dubbed when you add an anime
items.text: Anime now have an Audio choice when you add them. Dubbed only gets a release with both English and Japanese audio, and adds nothing if there isn't one. It plays in English from the start, and you can still switch in the Audio menu.

title: Add a whole show in one press

items.title: No season to choose
items.text: If someone already has a show here, Add to library now adds every episode they have straight away, across all seasons. To get anything else, press More episodes.

items.title: Ranges say what they're doing
items.text: A download of part of a season now shows which episodes are coming and how many are skipped, instead of looking like the whole season.

items.title: Ask for more episodes later
items.text: Asking for other episodes of a season uses the batch already on the server when it can, and skipped episodes now really start downloading.

items.title: Remove a show that's still downloading
items.text: You can now remove a show from your library while it's still downloading, and it stays gone. If someone else asked for it too, it carries on for them.

items.title: See how far it's come
items.text: The TV now shows progress wherever something's on its way: on the home screen, on a title's page, beside each episode and on cards in Discover. It tells you how many episodes are ready, too.

items.title: A home for documentaries
items.text: Discover has a new Documentaries tab, and it's on the TV's home screen too. Browse true crime, serial killers, unsolved cases, Swedish and Nordic documentaries, history, nature, science, music, sport and many more.

items.title: Free from SVT Play
items.text: SVT Play's documentaries and true crime are here now. Press Add and it lands in your library with Swedish subtitles, ready on every screen. Titles that the torrent sites don't have can often come from SVT Play instead. It only works in Sweden.

items.title: Better at finding things
items.text: Search looks in one more big source, and Swedish names with å, ä and ö find their releases more often. Search results also show what's on SVT Play.

title: See your downloads on the TV

items.title: On its way, in the library
items.text: Something you add on the TV now shows in your library straight away, in an On its way row with how far along it is. It moves to Films or Shows when it's ready.

items.title: Go to library
items.text: After you add a title on the TV, a Go to library button takes you straight to it.

items.title: Only what's in your library
items.text: Someone else's downloads no longer notify you about a show that isn't in your library, even if you follow it. Shows you have in your library still tell you about new episodes, and your own downloads still tell you when they're ready.

items.title: Choose your language
items.text: Lilin now speaks English and Swedish. Pick under Settings → Language and it applies everywhere: menus, the player, messages and notifications, on every device you sign in on. Descriptions and genres follow too, while titles keep their names.

items.title: One TV app, in Swedish
items.text: The new TV app with Discover, Search and genres has replaced the old one. It's in Swedish, and the on-screen keyboard has å, ä and ö.

items.title: Subtitles written by people come first
items.text: Lilin now always picks subtitles written by people when they exist. When only a machine translation exists, the language says “auto-translated” so you know what you’re getting, and it’s replaced automatically once people’s subtitles turn up.

items.title: Ready before you press play
items.text: When new episodes arrive or a season is upgraded, Lilin now finds their intros and credits in the background, so Skip intro and Up next are less likely to turn up late the first time you watch. Upgraded episodes also keep what was already found.

items.title: Fewer subtitles missed
items.text: The subtitle list could miss a language when a title had many subtitles in common languages. It now finds them. A language still only appears when someone has made subtitles in it for what you're watching.

items.title: Add instead of Download
items.text: Getting something new is now just Add: on a film, a show, a season or a single episode. If it's already here it's ready right away; otherwise it shows as On its way, then Almost ready, until you can press Play. A show you already watch says More episodes instead.

items.title: Georgian and Tagalog subtitles
items.text: Georgian and Tagalog are now in the subtitle list, next to the other languages, wherever someone has made them for what you're watching.

items.title: Proper episode titles
items.text: While an episode plays, the top of the player now shows the show's name and the episode's real title, like "House · Season 3, Episode 2: Cane & Able", instead of a short code like "house S03 E02".

items.title: Versions instead of double cards
items.text: If a film or an episode is here in two qualities, say 4K and 1080p, it now shows as one title instead of two. A Quality choice on the film's page, the season's page and in the player's quality menu picks which one plays. Your place carries over between them, on the website, TVs and Jellyfin. Phones start with the lighter version unless you pick another; your choice is remembered on each device.

items.title: No more accidental second copies
items.text: Downloading a film or episode you already have in the same quality is refused, with what's already here. Releases in a quality you have are marked in the release list. Another quality is fine: it becomes a version. A season pack only downloads the episodes you don't already have in that quality.

title: Better picture, and an Upgrade button

items.title: Best Quality means best picture
items.text: With Download quality set to Best Quality, Lilin used to pick the most popular release, and that is often a tiny re-encode that looks soft on a big screen. It now looks at how much picture a release really has (its size for the resolution, where it came from and who made it), so you get a proper BluRay or web release when one is out there. Balanced also skips releases that are far too small for their resolution.

items.title: Upgrade quality
items.text: Got a season that looks bad? Open Download on the show, pick the season and press Upgrade quality. Lilin looks for a clearly better release, downloads it, and swaps each episode for the new one as soon as it has finished. Your place in each episode carries over. If nothing better is out there, it tells you.

items.title: Names and I/l mix-ups fixed
items.text: Some releases come with subtitles that were read off the disc by a computer, so names and abbreviations show up in lowercase ("cuddy", "nicu") and I and l get swapped ("ls there", "l'm"). Lilin now fixes these in English subtitles as you watch, on the website, TVs and casting. It learns how names are spelled from the other subtitles in the library, so it gets better as the library grows.

items.title: Episodes 150 to 200
items.text: Long seasons (40 episodes or more, like Black Clover or One Piece) now have an Episodes choice in the Download panel. Pick "Choose a range", type the first and last episode, and only those download. A whole-season batch can still be used: the episodes outside your range are simply skipped.

items.title: One Piece numbering
items.text: One Piece's episodes keep their real numbers (Wano is episodes 892 to 1088), so downloads, the library and the episode list all agree. Searches no longer mix up the anime with the 2023 live-action series.

title: Stuck episodes no longer block a season

items.title: Seasons keep downloading
items.text: When a few episodes of a season can't find anyone to download from, the rest of the season now carries on instead of waiting behind them. A whole-season download also goes ahead of single episodes it already includes.

items.title: Anime downloads from Nyaa
items.text: Lilin now also searches Nyaa, where anime is released. Download Season on an anime picks a whole batch (one download for a season, even 170 episodes) instead of one torrent per episode, and finds single episodes whichever way they're numbered: "Black Clover - 176", "Black Clover 2nd Season - 06" and "S02E06" are all the same episode now.

items.title: Anime seasons line up
items.text: Anime that TMDB counts differently (Frieren's two seasons are one on TMDB, Jujutsu Kaisen's three seasons too) lands on the right season and episode in your library, under its proper name, and Lilin knows which episodes you already have so nothing downloads twice.

items.title: Subtitles on by default
items.text: If you've never picked subtitles, anime turns on the English subtitles it came with, so Japanese audio isn't left untranslated. Pick another language or Off in the player and that sticks as before.

items.title: Watch your library in Jellyfin
items.text: Got your own Jellyfin? Install the Lilin plugin there, open its settings and enter the code it shows under Settings → Jellyfin here. Your films and shows then appear in every Jellyfin app, and what you watch there shows up in Continue watching here too.

items.title: A lighter stream for big files on your phone
items.text: 4K films and other very large files used to stutter on phones. Now, on a phone, Lilin plays them as a lighter 1080p stream made on the fly, so they start fast and play smoothly, also on mobile data. The original file on the server stays exactly as it is.

items.title: Pick the quality yourself
items.text: The new quality button in the player (on phones and tablets) lets you choose Auto, Original, 1080p or 720p (a data saver). Your choice is remembered, and switching keeps your place in the video.

title: Browse and search on the TV (Preview)

items.title: A bigger Discover in Lilin Preview
items.text: In the Lilin Preview TV app, Discover rows now keep loading as you move along them, end in See all (a full grid), and are followed by a row of genres and one row per genre. Films / Shows tabs at the top narrow it down, and the title you're on fills the top of the screen with its description. Genre pages can be sorted by Popular, Top rated or Newest.

items.title: Search and genres on the TV
items.text: Lilin Preview has a Search screen with an on-screen keyboard (a real keyboard works too): your own titles show up at once, everything else from TMDB a moment later. Your library on the TV now also has a row for each genre you own something in.

items.title: Play on TV keeps your subtitles
items.text: Play on TV now starts with the same subtitles the player would turn on for you (your last language, or the one in Settings), so you don't have to pick them again in the TV remote. If they can't be fetched, the video starts without them. Apple TV still can't show subtitle files over AirPlay.

title: Player hints out of the way

items.title: Volume, sleep timer and skip hints
items.text: The little messages in the player (volume, sleep timer, skips, night mode and so on) now show just above the middle of the picture, so they no longer cover the play button or the loading ring on your phone. The play/pause flash stays in the middle, on the play button.

title: Agents can tap you on the shoulder

items.title: Notifications from your agents
items.text: A script or AI agent on your home machines can now send you a notification when it needs you. It uses the House token and only works from the home network. Turn it off under Settings › Notifications › Agents.

title: Browser copies can't fill a drive

items.title: Cache on any drive
items.text: The new CACHE_DIR setting in .env puts browser copies, timeline previews and share copies on a bigger drive than Lilin's own folder.

items.title: A cap and a safety margin
items.text: Browser copies stay under 150 GB (BROWSER_COPIES_MAX_GB); the ones nobody has watched for longest make room first. Conversions also leave 20 GB free on every drive (MIN_FREE_GB) and wait instead of filling it.

items.title: One library for the household
items.text: The owner can now let several people share one library. Everyone in it sees the same films and shows, on the TV too, and anyone can add, keep or remove titles. Your watch progress stays your own.

items.title: Set it in People
items.text: Settings → People has a Library choice for each person: Own library, or share with someone (joining someone who already shares joins the whole group).

items.title: Quieter library
items.text: The "Preparing playback" bar now only appears for videos in your library, and only when your browser actually needs that copy to play them. If you can already watch it, you won't see it.

items.title: Two conversions at once
items.text: Lilin now makes the quick copy for iPhone and Apple TV and the slower copy for older browsers at the same time, instead of one after the other. A new film no longer waits behind another film's long conversion.

items.title: Full quality in more browsers
items.text: If your browser plays HEVC (most do now, including Firefox on many PCs), you always get the original picture. The re-encoded copy is only used by browsers that can't play it.

title: Skip intro and Next episode on the TV

items.title: On your phone's TV remote
items.text: When you play an episode on the TV, the remote on your phone now shows Skip intro while the opening plays, and Up next once the credits start. Next episode starts it on the TV, with the same 10-second countdown as on the phone. Keep the remote open for the countdown: a locked phone can't start the next one.

items.title: Says what it's converting for
items.text: Some new films get a second, one-time copy that plays in every browser. The banner at the top of the library now says that, so it no longer looks like the same film is being converted twice. You can watch while it runs.

items.title: Trailers on title pages
items.text: Open a film or show in Discover and press Trailer on the picture at the top. The trailer plays right there, and stops when you close the page.

items.title: Adult content is blocked
items.text: Lilin no longer downloads porn. It's left out of torrent search, and links or .torrent files for it are refused. If a download turns out to contain it once it starts, it's removed straight away.

items.title: See who's sharing
items.text: Download details now show how many seeders a download is connected to, out of how many exist, like "12 of 340 seeders". The dot is lit when plenty are sharing and empty when nobody is, so you can tell a slow download from a stuck one.

items.title: Scroll with arrows
items.text: Continue watching in Library now has ← → buttons next to its title, like the rows in Discover. They only show when there are more cards than fit on screen.

items.title: Close stays in reach
items.text: The ✕ on sheets like this one now stays in the corner while you scroll, instead of scrolling away with the text.

items.title: Cleaner bottom edge
items.text: In What's new, text no longer peeks out below the Got it / Close button.

title: Faces, and a new Watch Together

items.title: Add your picture
items.text: Settings: tap the circle next to your name to add a profile picture. Drag it into place, zoom, save. It shows wherever your name does: Liked by, Popular on Lilin, watch parties, room chat and Wrapped.

items.title: Watch Together, redone
items.text: The room now opens as a panel beside the picture on bigger screens (a sheet on phones): everyone's face with a gold ring once they're ready, the host's crown, chat bubbles, one-tap invites with faces, and quick countdown buttons for the host. Invites look like a ticket and show who's already there.

items.title: Pictures for the family
items.text: In Settings → People, tap someone's circle to give them a picture (right-click to remove it).

items.title: Invite links work again
items.text: Since the sign-in update, opening an invite link and pressing Get access showed “This request came from another website”. That's fixed: invites you already sent work as they are.

items.title: Lilin Setup for Windows
items.text: Setting Lilin up on Windows no longer needs a terminal. Lilin Setup (in the Start menu, or LilinSetup.exe from the release page) walks you through your library, network, sign-in, services and start at boot, and checks your keys and ports as you go.

items.title: Game clips as an add-on
items.text: Turn on Clipper on the Game clips page: Setup installs it on this PC, or gives you one command to paste on your gaming PC and shares the clips folder for you.

items.title: Lilin in lights
items.text: Lilin has a new icon when you add it to your phone's home screen: a lit-up lilin M. On Android it now fills the icon shape properly instead of sitting in a white circle. Already added Lilin? Remove it from your home screen and add it again to get the new icon (iPhones keep the old one until you do).

items.title: Take it with you
items.text: Going somewhere without Wi-Fi? Open a film or episode and press To phone (the phone button on episode rows). Lilin makes a small copy (Small 480p, about 450 MB an hour, or Standard 720p) that plays in your phone's own video player with subtitles built in. Or download the file at full quality.

items.title: A whole season
items.text: Season to phone makes every episode of the season you're looking at. They're listed under For your phone in the Library, each with its own Download button as it's ready. With notifications on, you hear when one is done.

items.title: Phone copies
items.text: Copies are made one at a time with the GPU when it has NVENC, kept in cache/travel for 7 days after their last download (TRAVEL_KEEP_DAYS) and capped at 50 GB (TRAVEL_MAX_GB). HDR is tone-mapped to SDR.

items.title: Scrubbing looks the part
items.text: The picture you see while hovering or dragging along the timeline now sits in a small velvet card with the time in lilin gold, and a little pointer shows exactly where you'll land. While a preview is still loading, the card keeps its size instead of jumping.

items.title: Thumbs up, thumbs down
items.text: Rate any film or show from its page. Everyone sees who liked something ("Liked by Anna and Ben"); a thumbs down stays private.

items.title: Popular on Lilin
items.text: A new row near the top of Discover shows what people here liked and watched lately.

items.title: Chat and reactions in Watch Together
items.text: Open Room while watching together to send emoji that float over the picture, or chat. Messages pop up over the video, even with the controls hidden.

items.title: Plan a watch party
items.text: Pick a time from a film's or episode's page (the people icon) and send the invite. Everyone gets a countdown, and playback starts by itself for whoever's in the room. Your parties wait in Library. The host can also start a running room with a short countdown.

items.title: Lilin Wrapped
items.text: Settings → Lilin Wrapped tells the story of your year: hours watched, top titles, your show of the year, your busiest days and who you watched with. It counts from today on.

items.title: Your own password
items.text: Lilin can now sign you in by itself. If the owner made you an account, you'll see a sign-in page when you're away from home, and Settings lets you change your password or sign out.

items.title: Safer from other websites
items.text: Lilin now ignores requests that other websites try to send through your browser, so a page you visit can't start downloads or delete anything.

items.title: Server security
items.text: Create sign-ins with node setup.js user add EMAIL. Visitors from the internet always sign in; HOME_NETWORK_ACCESS=signin makes people at home sign in too. On Windows, run node setup.js service install once in an admin PowerShell: it removes the old SYSTEM watchdog task. Clipper installs are now pinned and checksum-verified.

items.title: Hear when it's ready
items.text: Turn on notifications in Settings and your phone or computer tells you when a download is ready to watch, even with Lilin closed.

items.title: New episodes
items.text: When a new episode of a show you follow or have in your library arrives on Lilin, you'll get a heads-up. Each kind of notification can be switched off on its own.

items.title: Invite people to watch
items.text: In a Watch Together room, tap Invite and pick someone: they get a notification that opens the room.

items.title: On iPhone
items.text: Apple only allows notifications for apps on the Home Screen: tap Share, then Add to Home Screen, and turn notifications on from there.

items.title: Save for later
items.text: Press Save on any film or show to keep it in a Saved for later row at the top of Discover.

items.title: Download when it's out
items.text: Saved a film that isn't out yet? Tick "Download it when a good copy is out" and it downloads by itself once it's released, never a cinema recording.

items.title: Follow a show
items.text: Press Follow on a show and each new episode downloads by itself once it has aired. Episodes you already had aren't fetched again, and older episodes are left alone.

items.title: New and Coming up
items.text: Episodes that arrived this way show a New badge on the show until you open it, and the Library has a Coming up row with the next episodes and release dates.

items.title: Skip the opening titles
items.text: A Skip intro button now appears while a show's opening titles play (or press S). Lilin finds the theme song by comparing an episode with its neighbours, so it works even after a long cold open.

items.title: Or skip them automatically
items.text: Settings → Watching → Intros can skip openings on their own. Rewind into one and it plays as normal.

items.title: Night mode
items.text: Tap the moon in the player (or press N) to even out loud explosions and quiet dialogue, with voices lifted so you can keep the volume down.

items.title: Sleep timer
items.text: Also under the moon: pause after 15 minutes to an hour and a half, with the sound fading out gently, or at the end of the episode so the next one doesn't start while you sleep.

items.title: Subtitles your way
items.text: The subtitles menu now sets the style (a dark box, a soft shadow or an outline) and how high the lines sit, as well as the size.

items.title: Two languages at once
items.text: Pick a Second language in the subtitles menu to show it above the first. Handy for learning a language, or when you're watching with someone who reads another.

items.title: What's new, right here
items.text: From now on, Lilin shows you what changed after each update, just like this. You can read past updates any time in Settings → What's new.

items.title: Next episode starts with the credits
items.text: When the credits roll, an Up next card counts down and plays the next episode. Pause or tap Keep watching to stay where you are.

items.title: Stats for nerds
items.text: Press I while watching, or right-click the picture, to see everything about the stream: resolution, codecs, HDR, bitrate, dropped frames, buffer and download speed. Copy puts it all on your clipboard.

items.title: Previews while you seek
items.text: Drag along the timeline to see a small picture of that moment before you let go.

items.title: Subtitles that line up
items.text: Subtitles are checked against the audio and fixed when they drift, even when they were made for a different cut of the film.

items.title: Always up to date
items.text: Finished downloads, deletions and where you stopped watching on another device now show up straight away, without reloading.

items.title: Add to library
items.text: If someone else already has a title on the server, Download becomes Add to library: it's yours instantly, with nothing to wait for.

items.title: Exact clip cuts
items.text: Game clips can now be cut on any frame, not just the nearest keyframe, with no loss in quality.

title: Episode pictures and a tidier library

items.title: A picture for every episode
items.text: Episodes now show a still from the episode itself in the season list, Continue watching and Up next, so you can spot the one you want at a glance.

items.title: Delete a season or a whole show
items.text: A show's page can remove one season or the whole show in one go, instead of episode by episode.

items.title: Ready to play sooner
items.text: New downloads are prepared for playing about twice as fast, and Firefox gets its own copy straight away instead of when you press Play.

items.title: Tidier subtitles
items.text: Subtitle lines no longer crowd into each other, and long lines stop wrapping too early in Firefox.

items.title: Steadier TV casting
items.text: Play on TV keeps playing the file it started with, even if the library changes underneath it.

items.title: Notes on your phone
items.text: Notes fit small screens now: easy-to-tap actions with undo, the keyboard no longer covers what you're typing, and images open full screen.

items.title: Search inside images
items.text: Text in note images (screenshots, receipts, posters) is read automatically, so a search finds them too.

items.title: Notes and clips in Discord
items.text: A shared note shows as a preview card in Discord with its images or video. Shared clips open in Lilin's own player, at full quality.

items.title: Better clip editing
items.text: Cut several parts out of a clip in one edit, and leave out audio tracks you don't want, like a noisy mic.

items.title: House: Sharing and Screen Time
items.text: House → Sharing shows what streams and encodes cost the server right now. Screen Time shows how long each computer at home has been used, and on what.

items.title: Download in one press
items.text: Download picks the best release for you from your quality setting, size limit and audio language. For a show, choose the season and press Download Season.

items.title: Episodes in order
items.text: Episode one downloads first and at full speed, so you can start watching while the rest of the season finishes.

items.title: 1440p
items.text: Between 1080p and 4K, there's now a 1440p choice for sharp pictures without 4K's size.

items.title: One library
items.text: Downloads show on the title's own card in your library, episode by episode, as soon as each one is ready.

items.title: A library that keeps itself current
items.text: New downloads and changes appear in the library on their own, and when an episode ends, Lilin offers the next one.

items.title: Notes
items.text: A shared Notes tab for messages, links, photos and videos. Photos and videos uploaded from a phone stay private to Lilin.

items.title: Rename clips
items.text: Give a clip a proper name instead of the recorder's timestamp.

items.title: Your own account
items.text: Everyone signs in to their own Lilin: your library, where you stopped and your settings are yours. If someone else already has a title on the server, add it to your library instead of downloading it again.

items.title: Settings
items.text: A Settings tab for colour themes, default subtitles, preferred quality, the page Lilin opens on and how your library is sorted.

items.title: Watch Together
items.text: Start a room from the player and send the link: playback stays in sync for everyone, and each person picks their own subtitles. Links show a preview in Discord.

items.title: Shows by season
items.text: Shows appear once in your library with their seasons and episode names. When there's no good season download, Lilin gets it episode by episode.

items.title: Library clean-up
items.text: Videos leave your library 7 days after they finish downloading unless you tap Keep, so old downloads don't pile up on the server.

items.title: Arrows on Discover
items.text: Rows on Discover have arrows, so you can scroll them with a mouse.

items.title: House
items.text: The House tab shows the server's disks, downloads and services, plus the computers at home. Wake the gaming PC and pick Linux or Windows, or restart it into the other.

items.title: Clips
items.text: Game clips from the PC, grouped by game, with share links that play right inside Discord. Trim them without losing quality, or delete the ones you don't want.

items.title: Invite links
items.text: Make a one-time invite link in Activity: the person enters their email and gets access, no dashboard needed.

items.title: New player controls
items.text: A seek bar that shows how much has loaded and the time under your finger, volume that's remembered, and everything in one row. On phones, double-tap left or right to skip 10 seconds.

items.title: Subtitles that make room
items.text: Subtitles are sized to the picture and move just far enough to clear the controls while they show. On an upright phone they sit in the empty space below the picture.

items.title: Keyboard shortcuts
items.text: Space to pause, arrows to skip and change volume, F for fullscreen, C for subtitles and more. Press ? while watching to see them all.

items.title: Pause or remove downloads
items.text: Downloads can be paused, resumed or deleted from their card.

items.title: Plays in Firefox
items.text: Browsers that can't play HEVC video, like Firefox, get a copy they can play, made automatically.

items.title: Subtitles fix themselves
items.text: Subtitles are lined up with the audio automatically when they're out of sync.

items.title: Nudge subtitles
items.text: If a line still shows up early or late, shift the subtitles in small steps from the player.

items.title: Safari and iPhone
items.text: Videos now play in Safari on Mac, iPhone and iPad.

items.title: Theater mode
items.text: In theater mode the player bar hides itself and the video sits in the middle of the screen.

items.title: One remote
items.text: When you cast to a TV, the remote shows only on the device that started it.

items.title: Activity log
items.text: The owner can see what happened on the server: who watched, downloaded and deleted what.

items.title: AirPlay and Chromecast
items.text: Send a film or episode to your TV at full quality.

items.title: Home TVs stay at home
items.text: The TVs at home are only offered when you're on the home network.

items.title: Ready sooner
items.text: New downloads are picked up for playing every 30 seconds instead of every two minutes.

items.title: Welcome to Lilin
items.text: Find films and shows, download them to the server and stream them in your browser, on any device.
